# Talk to Hardware Recipe

## Problem

Developers can understand a voice-AI hardware build faster when they can talk to a live assistant while inspecting the device. The app combines Agora's realtime conversation pipeline with a full-screen white-lab procedural ESP32-S3 teardown visualizer.

## Architecture

```text
Browser microphone
        |
Agora RTC + RTM
        |
Gemini STT -> Gemini LLM -> MiniMax TTS
        |
Agora RTC audio response
```

The 3D visualization is a separate client-side state machine:

```text
User speech transcript
        |
local command mapper
        |
validated HardwareCommand
        |
VisualizerState
        |
React Three Fiber hardware scene
```

## Agora Responsibilities

Agora owns the realtime voice experience:

- RTC channel connection
- RTM transcript/state/metrics events
- token generation
- Conversational AI agent invitation
- agent lifecycle and stop flow
- microphone publishing
- agent audio playback
- managed MiniMax TTS

The existing voice pipeline remains:

```text
Microphone -> Gemini STT -> Gemini LLM -> MiniMax TTS -> Agora RTC -> Browser
```

## Gemini Responsibilities

Gemini owns conversational reasoning in the voice pipeline. The default LLM model is `gemini-3.6-flash`, isolated behind `NEXT_GEMINI_LLM_MODEL` so a newer supported model identifier can be swapped in later without touching app code.

## Hardware Visualizer Workflow

The first screen renders `components/hardware/HardwareVisualizer.tsx`, backed by metadata and reducer logic in `lib/hardware.ts`. The layout reserves a large white 3D workbench for the hardware and a separate side panel for voice controls, suggested prompts, selected-part details, and transcript. The visualizer includes an ESP32-S3, mini breadboard, microphone array, camera module, audio board, speaker, power, controls, wiring, and enclosure parts.

Exploded mode should stay camera-bounded. Prefer compact layered teardown positions over wide horizontal spreads that push components out of frame.

Supported visual commands:

- `explode`
- `assemble`
- `focus_component`
- `show_all`
- `show_minimum`
- `show_audio_flow`
- `reset_view`

Commands can come from manual UI controls or completed user transcript turns. The app validates commands before applying them and never allows arbitrary JavaScript execution from LLM output.

## Voice -> Visual Action

`components/ConversationComponent.tsx` receives transcript updates from `AgoraVoiceAI`. Completed user turns are passed to `LandingPage`, which uses `createCommandFromText()` to map natural language into a `HardwareCommand`.

Examples:

- "Show me the microphone" -> `focus_component` with `microphone`
- "Explode the device" -> `explode`
- "Put it back together" -> `assemble`
- "Show the minimum setup" -> `show_minimum`
- "How does my voice reach the AI?" -> `show_audio_flow`

The agent still answers conversationally through the Agora voice path. Visual command metadata is local-only and must not be spoken as raw JSON.

## Extension Ideas

- Replace the local text mapper with formal provider tool calls when the Agora/Gemini provider path exposes a suitable structured metadata channel.
- Add real hardware images or a GLTF model while keeping the procedural fallback.
- Add wiring annotations for a specific ESP32-S3 dev kit.
- Add authenticated session ownership for production deployments.
